Production order

Make a finished item on a production order from stock you already hold, and check that on-hand rose by what you made.

Before you start

  • A finished item with a BOM and a routing, and its components in stock. Purchase to receipt buys components in.
  • The finished item has a BOM and a routing, and each component has stock in a warehouse. Build the job shop bill of material, Build the job shop routing and Stock the components make them.

Procedure

1Confirm the existing foundation

Result
The finished item, its components and their on-hand are written down.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes yet. A production order uses master data that must already exist, and LN fills the BOM, routing and warehouse in from it. The proof at the end is the finished item's on-hand going up, and that needs the figure from before.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Inventory 360One row for each item
1.2Above the grid's Item column are two filter boxes; the first, small one is for a project. Type the finished item in the second and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.3Tick the item's own row and click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory opens, one row per warehouseWrite downfinished itemreceiving warehousefinished item on-hand before
1.4Close that tab, untick the row, and do the same for each componentWrite downcomponent warehousecomponent on-hand before
Confirm the existing foundation: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Warehouse Inventory opens Warehouse - Item Inventory Ownership insteadA warehouse is set in Filter Items. Clear Site and Warehouse, click Refresh, and tick the row again
A component has no stockStock it first. Purchase to receipt buys it in

2Create the production order

Result
A production order for the finished item is saved, with status Created.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. LN fills most of the order in from the item: the BOM and the receiving warehouse when you enter it, and the routing when you enter the quantity. On save it builds the order's operations and materials from them. Nothing moves yet.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Production OrdersThe list of production orders
2.2Click NewProduction Order opens, empty, with Site filled in
2.3Item has two boxes. Leave the first, for a project, empty. Type the finished item in the second and press TabExampleItem BAM-CHOP-PAIRThe item's description fills in, with BOM, its revision and Warehouse
2.4Press Tab to reach Quantity Ordered, type the quantity to make, and press TabExampleQuantity Ordered 1Routing and its revision fill inWrite downproduction quantity
2.5Check WarehouseThe receiving warehouse
2.6Click SaveProduction Order shows the new number, Order Status CreatedWrite downproduction order number
Create the production order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
BOM or Routing stays emptyThe item may have no BOM or routing valid today. Stop, and check them with whoever maintains the item
The item code is cut shortIt went into the project box. Clear both boxes and type it in the second
LN says Enter a value for the Quantity Ordered field.The typing didn't reach the field, and the form may stop responding. Discard the order, reload LN and start again, reaching the field by Tab
The form stops respondingDiscard the order and reload LN

3Verify the generated foundation

Result
The order's operations and materials are the ones you expect.

Why LN works this way. On save LN copied the routing's operations and the BOM's materials onto the order, scaled to its quantity. A missing operation or material here is a reason to stop, not something to fix in the order.

StepActionYou should see
3.1On the order, open the Operations tabOne line per operation, with its work center
3.2Open the Materials tabOne line per component, with its estimated quantity and warehouse
3.3Check each component's warehouseThe component warehouse
3.4Read Order StatusCreated. Nothing is released or issued yet
Verify the generated foundation: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No operations, or no materialsThe routing or BOM wasn't found. Leave the order at Created and check the item's master data
A component comes from another warehouseLN takes the warehouse from the item's setup. Check that warehouse has the stock, or stop

4Release the order

Result
The order is Released, with a warehousing order to issue the materials and one to receive the finished item.

Why LN works this way. Release lets production start. At the same moment LN makes two warehousing orders under the production order's number: an issue order to move the materials to the work center, and a receipt order to bring the finished item into its warehouse. Both wait until you start them.

StepActionYou should see
4.1On the order's toolbar, click Release Order…Release Production Orders opens for this order
4.2Click ReleaseThe dialog closes. Order Status = Released
4.3Open Warehousing Orders
4.4Type the production order number in the filter box above the Order column and press EnterTwo rows, both Planned: a Receipt to the receiving warehouse, and an Issue from the component warehouse to a work center
Release the order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The order doesn't reach ReleasedRead the message. Release may need the documents printed first; see the note
No warehousing orders are listedCheck the number in the filter, and that the order reads Released

5Issue material to the job shop

Result
The materials are shipped to the work center, and the order is Active.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. The issue order waits until you start the issue. Starting it opens the issue order's lines, and shipping them takes the materials out of their warehouse. The first material shipped makes the order Active; release alone doesn't.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Open Production Orders and tick the order
5.2Choose Actions➔Materials➔Initiate Inventory Issue…Initiate Inventory Issue opens
5.3In To Date/Time, pick a day after the order's production start with the calendarExampleTo Date/Time The day after the production startThe date changes
5.4Click Initiate, then ContinueProcess completed. in the status bar. The dialog stays open
5.5Click Close, and on Production Orders choose Actions➔Materials➔Material to Issue for Production OrdersOne line per component. To Issue by Warehouse = its estimated quantity
5.6Tick a line and choose References➔Warehouse OrdersWarehousing Orders. The issue order reads Open
5.7On the issue order's row, click Drill InWarehousing Order, with one outbound line per component, each Open
5.8On the Outbound Lines tab, tick every line and choose Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceEach line reads Advised
5.9Tick every line again and choose Actions➔Advice➔Release AdviceEach line, and the order, reads Shipped
5.10Go back to Material to Issue for Production Orders and click RefreshActual Quantity = the estimated quantity, To Issue by Warehouse = 0. The order reads Active
Issue material to the job shop: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
To Issue by Warehouse stays 0 after step 5.4To Date/Time may be before the materials are due. Run step 5.2 again with a later date
The issue stops short and a shortage report printsA component is short and negative stock isn't allowed. The quantity waits in To Issue by Warehouse; restock it, then go on from step 5.6
A Loading badge stays over the lines' Actions buttonClick Refresh on the Outbound Lines toolbar
Lines are already Advised or ShippedThe material is set to process by itself. Go on to step 5.10

6Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt

Result
The order reads Production Completed, and the finished item's on-hand rose by the quantity made.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. Two reports finish the order. Reporting the operation records what was made. Reporting the order delivers it to the receiving warehouse, and your answer to one question decides whether Warehousing has to receive it by hand. The on-hand figure is the proof the stock arrived.

StepActionYou should see
6.1On Production Orders, tick the order and choose Actions➔Report Operations CompletedOne line per operation, Active
6.2Double-click the operation's Additional Completed and type the production quantityExampleAdditional Completed 1
6.3Click SaveCumulative Completed = the production quantity. The operation is still Active
6.4Tick the operation and click Complete on the toolbarOperation Status = Completed
6.5Back on Production Orders, with the order still ticked, choose Actions➔Report Orders CompletedReport Orders Completed opens, with the receiving warehouse
6.6Type the production quantity in Additional Quantity to Deliver and click SaveExampleAdditional Quantity to Deliver 1LN asks: Automatically confirm receipt when activating warehouse order inbound line?
6.7Click YesDelivered = the production quantity, Quantity to Deliver = 0
6.8Set Order Status to Production Completed and click SaveCompletion Date fills in
6.9On Production Orders, click RefreshOrder Status = Production Completed
6.10Open Inventory 360, filter the finished item, tick its row and click Warehouse InventoryThe receiving warehouse's on-hand rose by the production quantityWrite downfinished item on-hand after
Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Complete is greyed outTick the operation's row first
Report Orders Completed has nothing to deliverThe operation isn't Completed yet. Go back to step 6.4
Quantity to Deliver keeps the quantityYou answered No. Receive the receipt order in Warehousing, then read the on-hand
On-hand didn't go upCheck Delivered on Report Orders Completed, and that the receipt order reads Received

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
More than one operationEach operation is reported complete in turn, in Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt
Materials set to issue by themselvesWith Direct Initiate Inventory Issue and Direct Process Warehouse Order Line set, release ships the materials, and most of Issue material to the job shop is already done
Receiving by handAnswering No to the receipt question leaves the finished item for Warehousing to receive on the receipt order
No routingOutside this guide. Without a routing, no estimated production costs are defined
More than one operation
Task 3		Each one is reported in Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt, in sequence
More than one operation
Task 6		Do steps 6.2–6.4 for each operation, in sequence, before step 6.5
